description:
Studentship Overview

King's Business School invites applications for funded, full-time PhD studentships to start in the 2027-2028 academic year. We welcome applicants interested in undertaking research in any of our areas of expertise. Our PhD programmes include Economics Research (Accounting & Financial Management, Banking & Finance, Economics) and Management Research (Human Resource Management & Employment Relations, Marketing, Public Services Management & Organisation, Strategy, International Management & Entrepreneurship).

Funding and Benefits

  • Home/EU and International studentships are available to students with outstanding research potential.
  • Studentships cover tuition fees for three years, the pending submission status fee, and a tax-free stipend of approximately £23,805 per annum (2027-2028 rate) for four years with small, annual inflationary increases.
  • Students are expected to undertake some teaching and/or marking activities in the School. Any teaching undertaken will attract payment in addition to the stipend.
  • Students also have access to a generous training and conference fund.

Eligibility Criteria

  • All applicants for the full-time PhD programme are eligible to apply, including Home, EU and International students.
  • You will be required to live in the UK throughout your full-time studies, although it is understood that you may need to spend short periods overseas while conducting fieldwork.

Application Process

  1. Identify potential supervisors who are willing to supervise you. Supervisors will ask to have an interview with you. State in the interview that you would like to be considered for the King's Business School Doctoral Studentship.
  2. Complete an application to the relevant PhD programme via King's Apply. Applicants should have identified a potential supervisor and should have had an interview before submitting the application.
  3. The studentship deadline is 1st December 2026 at 17.00.

Assessment Criteria

  • Evidence of the candidate's individual research potential (references, academic transcripts, prizes, awards, publications, professional qualifications, relevant experience).
  • The quality and fit of the proposed research (well-formulated topic and questions, feasible plan of action, genuine scope for doctoral research, fit with research group/School/College, potential for societal or economic impact).

About King's College London

King's College London is a public research university and a Russell Group member. Its undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes span medicine, law, humanities, psychology, science and other disciplines. With campuses across central London, King's connects academic study and research with healthcare institutions, cultural organisations and wider questions affecting contemporary society.

Official website: https://www.kcl.ac.uk/

Important Notes

  • Studentships cover tuition fees for three years and a tax-free stipend for four years.
  • Teaching activities are expected and paid in addition to the stipend.
  • Applicants must have identified a supervisor and had an interview before applying.
  • Open to Home, EU and International students.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 1 December 2026, 17:00 GMT. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
